java_locations.role: Selects an entity BACK color before the merged class style and copies that selected color to HEADER when no explicit header color exists, so one inline gradient paints the complete class body without a distinct header repaint.
Interns gradients lazily by the ordered color1/color2/policy tuple, assigns source-seeded ids at first paint, and maps the four policies to SVG endpoints.
Carries the two colors and orientation policy as one paint value rather than flattening the first color during model resolution.

rust_locations.role: Retains the complete inline class color, including its gradient separator and second color.
Registers gradients from class and header style backgrounds only; entity inline gradient values are absent from the resource inventory.
Detects that an inline entity color is a gradient but resolves it to its first color because no matching generated definition or selected gradient fill is supplied.

claimed_invariant: Class background paint is selected per entity before SVG resource generation: an inline BACK color overrides the merged class background style, and when HEADER is absent that same selected paint applies to the whole class. A gradient remains a typed two-color/policy paint through selection. The SVG backend interns each distinct selected gradient tuple at first entity paint, reuses its id for duplicates, and emits no separate header repaint when header and body are the same inline gradient.
causal_divergence: The frozen input has two inline class gradients. Java selects those entity BACK values, lazily registers two gradient resources, and paints each complete class rectangle with its corresponding url. Rust parses both values intact but class_gradients inventories only global classBackgroundColor and classHeaderBackgroundColor. With no definitions available, render_entity_content deliberately flattens each inline gradient to its first color. The six missing SVG elements are exactly the two linearGradient nodes and their four stops; class geometry is otherwise generated by the ordinary class layout model.
planned_model_change: Build the class gradient resource inventory from the paint selected for each entity in source paint order. For each entity, prefer its inline color over its source-epoch merged class background; also register a distinct source-epoch header gradient when selected. Deduplicate by canonical color1/color2/policy while preserving first paint order. Resolve the entity-selected body gradient against that inventory before shape emission, preserving the existing flat-color and style precedence. Add fresh tests spanning all policies, duplicate reuse, renamed entities, declaration counts, and inline-over-style precedence.

It does not alter class geometry, layout ordering, gradient id hashing, note gradients, parser grammar, comparator behavior, golden data, or fixture eligibility.

experimental_result.accepted_result: edge_color_gradient becomes structurally equivalent through render_svg without oracle input. The frozen shipped-path census rises from 11,165/11,251 to 11,166/11,251, with edge-cases moving from 754/777 to 755/777 and every other family unchanged.
experimental_result.model_evidence: The generated class resource inventory now follows SVEK entity emission order and selects each entity's inline BACK color before its merged class style. Inline paint is copied to the header selection, while a style-selected body can retain a distinct header gradient. Resource identity includes canonical color1, color2, and policy. Fresh renamed inputs exercise all four policies, five declarations, duplicate tuple reuse, and inline-over-global-style precedence. The perturbation also confirmed Java's legacy skinparam refresh behavior: the final global class background applies retroactively, while the inline entity color still wins.
experimental_result.review_status: Implemented and locally verified; independent adversarial review and Java-generated held-outs remain pending because checker capacity and the local Java runtime are unavailable. This record does not self-attest acceptance.
